text:
incident-bot: Paging: Elevated 504/502 gateway errors observed for inference-gateway in private VPC peering (peering-transit-1). alert: gateway_5xx_rate > 2% (5m). Affected: dedicated customers behind transit-appliance. Severity: P1.
oncall-lee: i'm on it. on-call handover from eng-sre-bot received. grabbing dashboard and ssh keys.
alex-k: seeing a sharp spike in 504s at ~21:11 UTC. gateway-proxy logs show downstream TCP timeouts to 10.240.2.0/24 (transit-side). lots of SYN->SYN-ACK mismatches.
maya-s: can someone pull NAT / conntrack metrics for the transit appliance and the nat gateway? suspect ephemeral port exhaustion or asymmetric SNAT.
ryan-sre: /cc opsbot run: describe nat usage + conntrack on transit-host. also get VPC flow logs for the peering interface.
opsbot: nat-gw nat-03a: ephemeral ports used 98%. active connections: 8.7k. conntrack table: 93,412 entries (soft threshold 100k). 5xx spike correlates with ephemeral ports near capacity.
alex-k: that explains the 504s — new outbound connections can't get SNAT ports, downstream drops, gateway returns 504. traffic pattern: a customer load test started at 21:08 hitting many hosts concurrently.
oncall-lee: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce client concurrency (rate-limit at gateway) 2) add a second NAT gateway / SNAT pool for affected subnets 3) rotate route table to prefer new NAT 4) clear conntrack stale entries if needed.
maya-s: i'm applying a temporary rate-limit on the inference route (api-gateway): throttling concurrent requests to 60% for the dedicated tier. config snippet pushed: 
```
# envoy rate limit (temp)
route_config:
  - match: /v1/inference
    per_connection_limit: 200
    concurrency_limit: 120
```

alex-k: also running quick checks on pods: `kubectl -n infra exec -it gateway-proxy-1 -- ss -tan | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` -> 8123 TIME_WAIT. lots of short lived conns.
ryan-sre: launching new NAT gateway in us-east-1a (nat-04) and associating EIP. will attach to peering route for affected subnets. command: `aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0a --allocation-id eipalloc-0bb` (started).
opsbot: created nat-04 (pending). once available will update route table rtb-0peering to point 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-04 for subnets: infra-subnet-1a, customer-subnet-1a.
customer-success: heads-up — customer cust-42 reported intermittent 504s and raised a ticket. communicating that we're mitigating now.
alex-k: while nat-04 is provisioning, i'm going to drop conntrack entries older than 600s on transit-host to free ephemeral ports: `sudo conntrack -D --timeout 600` (will do with caution).
oncall-lee: please ensure we don't break established flows. prefer route swap + concurrency throttle first.
ryan-sre: nat-04 is now available. updating route table to route affected subnets via nat-04.
opsbot: route update applied to rtb-0peering. traffic should begin egressing via nat-04 within a minute.
eng-sre-bot: metrics: gateway_5xx_rate reduced from 2.4% -> 0.6% within 3 minutes of rate-limit + route swap.
alex-k: confirmed connection failures dropping. TCP retransmits and RSTs decreased in gateway logs.
maya-s: removed the emergency conntrack purge — not needed. leaving conntrack conservative.
oncall-lee: handoff: i'm going to coordinate postmortem with ryan-sre and eng-sre. ryan, you'll own the remediation (add autoscale for SNAT / additional NAT pool + tagging + alerting).
ryan-sre: ack. immediate follow-ups: (1) autoscale NAT capacity doc + runbook (2) add a monitoring alert when ephemeral port usage > 85% (3) evaluate upstream client throttling and burst-smoothing.
customer-success: notified cust-42 of mitigation and ETA for postmortem. they reported service returned to normal.
eng-sre-bot: final check: 5xx rate back to baseline 0.2% at 21:35 UTC. closing real-time paging.
oncall-lee: closing incident channel for now. we'll open a postmortem doc and include timeline, root cause (ephemeral SNAT port exhaustion caused by unthrottled customer test + single NAT pool), mitigations, and action items. thanks all :thumbsup:
alex-k: adding a quick note for postmortem: consider per-customer egress pools or source IP preservation for high-throughput customers to avoid shared SNAT exhaustion.
ryan-sre: will schedule follow-up with infra-networking to investigate peering path optimizations and connection reuse strategies.
opsbot: checklist created: [create additional NAT pools, alert on ephemeral usage, add circuit-breaker at gateway, postmortem].
customer-success: customer updated and happy to sync after postmortem.
oncall-lee: handing to ryan-sre for post-incident and action tracking. leaving channel. :white_check_mark:
